technologies.how: Inductive types, dependent functions, propositions, tactics, and theorem elaboration.
technologies.name: Lean 4
technologies.what: Combines dependent types, executable functional programming, and machine-checked proofs.
technologies.when: Use when a critical property must be proven rather than sampled by tests.
technologies.where: Safety invariants, receipt-chain correctness, mathematics, and verified decision gates.
technologies.why: It produces kernel-checked proofs with explicit assumptions and reusable theorem libraries.

technologies.how: Inductive types, propositions, tactics, dependent records, modules, and extraction.
technologies.name: Coq
technologies.what: Defines programs and machine-checked proofs in the Calculus of Inductive Constructions.
technologies.when: Use when constructive proofs, extraction, or mature proof libraries fit the assurance case.
technologies.where: Verified compilers, protocols, cryptography, semantics, and critical algorithms.
technologies.why: It checks every proof term with a small trusted kernel and can extract verified programs.

technologies.how: Indexed data types, pattern matching, modules, implicit arguments, and termination checking.
technologies.name: Agda
technologies.what: Uses dependent types for proofs and total functional programs.
technologies.when: Use when the implementation and proof should inhabit the same expressive dependent type system.
technologies.where: Protocol models, type-safe DSLs, mathematical structures, and certified transformations.
technologies.why: It makes invariants part of types and requires total, structurally valid definitions.
